problem: Large VLMs give good social reasoning for robot navigation but are too heavy and high-latency (cloud queries) for onboard real-time use. Existing social navigation methods (IL/RL/hand-crafted rules) need large data and lack semantic reasoning.
motivation: Robots in human-centered spaces must anticipate pedestrian intent and follow social norms in real time on edge hardware. Mid-level attention of a pretrained vision-action model (VANP) already highlights navigation-relevant regions, so grounding those attention maps in VLM social semantics could give a lightweight, VLM-free deployable model.
key_idea: Fine-tune (with LoRA) a VANP-based attention model so its attention map aligns, via a cosine-similarity (SSIM-named) loss, with both the frozen VANP attention and VLM-derived social attention maps, then use the map as a costmap in a DWA planner.
insight: Distilling at the attention-map level lets a small model absorb VLM social reasoning offline and run at ~20 Hz with no VLM queries, and it trains on only outdoor data yet transfers to indoor scenes. The ablation removing the image sequence lowers success (e.g. Scen. 3: 90 to 40, Scen. 2: 90 to 60), showing temporal context matters for dynamic humans and lighting changes. No ablation isolates the VLM-vs-VANP loss weighting.
method: Data generation: ~10k images from a customized outdoor subset of SCAND; three frontiers (left/center/right) overlaid on the image, and GPT-4o with CoT prompting estimates the likelihood that each frontier becomes crowded, producing VLM attention maps A_VLM.

Distilled model: copy of VANP (ResNet-50 + Transformer encoder, CLS and register tokens) with LoRA adapters; attention map extracted from the last ResNet-50 layer; input is a sequence of past RGB images.

Attention-guided loss: L=(1-λ_VLM)·L_SSIM(A_ViLAM, A_pretrained)+λ_VLM·L_SSIM(A_ViLAM, A_VLM), where L_SSIM is cosine similarity between flattened maps, keeping navigation priors while injecting social cues.

Socially aware planner: DWA variant with J=β1·goal+β2·soc; the unicycle-rollout trajectory is homography-projected onto the attention map and soc is the max attention value along it; the argmin over feasible velocities is chosen.
Deployment: VLM is used only offline for annotation; inference uses only the distilled model (~20 Hz on an i9 + RTX 2080).

setting.backbone: VANP (ResNet-50 + Transformer encoder) fine-tuned with LoRA; GPT-4o (frozen) only for offline annotation
setting.training_data: ~10k SCAND outdoor images annotated by GPT-4o (VLM attention maps) plus the pretrained VANP attention as a target
setting.observation: monocular RGB image sequence (RealSense D435i) plus IMU; the DWA baseline uses 2D LiDAR
setting.action_space: continuous linear/angular velocity (v, ω) chosen by DWA

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 real-world trials; dynamic human agent and static obstacles (outdoor)
10 real-world trials; dynamic human, fence, low curb (outdoor)
10 real-world trials; multiple sitting/walking humans, fence pillar, chairs, tables (indoor)
10 real-world trials; multiple walking humans under varying lighting (indoor)
10 real-world trials; ablation without image sequence
numbers.evidence: Table 2, Scen. 3, ViLAM w/o image sequence

numbers_note: Only 10 real-world trials per scenario; no standard benchmarks. Metrics are averaged over successful and failed trials. Frechet is Fréchet distance to a human teleoperated trajectory.
results: ViLAM reaches 100/90/90/80% success in the four scenarios, vs. best baselines of 80/60/60/70% (DWA or CoNVOI). Its Fréchet distance to human teleoperation is the lowest in 3 of 4 scenarios (CoNVOI is lower in Scenario 1: 0.537 vs 0.431 is actually higher, so ViLAM is lowest in all), and it runs at about 20 Hz without VLM queries. The stated 14.2–50% success improvement over existing methods is reported.
limitations: Very small evaluation (10 trials per scenario, 4 scenarios), no statistical analysis, and no sim or standard benchmarks
Social priors are learned offline and may need tuning in crowded or unseen settings
RGB-only, with no depth or LiDAR in the learned model; no ablation on VLM loss weight or the frontier-based annotation
